expectations.text: States the intended reader and what they already know, in frontmatter or the opening
expectations.evidence: Frontmatter line 3: 'audience: Frontend engineers new to the team. Know Docker and GitHub Actions well; have never seen the staging cluster, Vault or the preview setup.'

expectations.text: The first paragraph tells the reader that every PR gets a preview environment and where to find it (the pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev URL)
expectations.evidence: Line 8-11: 'Every pull request gets its own running copy of the web app at `https://pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev`, about 6 minutes after each push.'

expectations.text: Does not explain Docker basics such as what an image or a container is
expectations.evidence: Only 'Builds the Docker image from the repository.' No definition of image or container.

expectations.text: Explains Vault, or the secret/preview/web path, at first use in words a reader new to it can act on
expectations.evidence: Line 46-48 at first use: 'Vault is where the platform team stores secrets... If your change needs a new secret, ask the platform team to add it under `secret/preview/web`.'

expectations.text: Explains mailhog, or what happens to emails in a preview, at first use
expectations.evidence: Line 41 at first use: 'every email the app sends goes to MailHog, a mail catcher. Read it at https://pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev/mailhog.'

expectations.text: Omits the story of trying ephemeral databases first, or reduces it to a single sentence of rationale
expectations.evidence: No mention of ephemeral databases or seeded fixtures anywhere.

expectations.text: Writes the concurrent-push failure with the condition (two pushes within about a minute) before the instruction (re-run the job)
expectations.evidence: Line 65-66: 'If two pushes land within about a minute of each other, the second Helm install fails ... Re-run the failed `preview` job' - condition precedes instruction.

expectations.text: States what the reader cannot do: no ssh, and kubectl exec needs staging access most developers lack
expectations.evidence: Line 54-56: 'You cannot SSH into a preview. If you have access to the staging cluster, you can open a shell with `kubectl -n previews exec`; most developers do not have that access'.

expectations.text: Every heading names its content specifically, and no heading is directly followed by another heading
expectations.evidence: All headings are specific statements (e.g. 'The `preview` action deploys each push in about 6 minutes', 'Two pushes within a minute fail the second deploy'); every heading is followed by body text.
